blocks.title: What is this file?
blocks.what: The first object is the stable Deployment, the version most users get. It comes from apps/v1.
blocks.why: A canary sends a small share of traffic to a new version first. If it fails, few users notice.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because it cannot tell what you want to create.
blocks.comment: What to create first: the stable Deployment

blocks.title: Name the stable copy
blocks.why: Each version gets its own Deployment, so you can size them separately.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because every object needs a name.
blocks.comment: The Deployment for the stable version
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: store-stable

blocks.title: Nine stable Pods
blocks.what: Keep nine stable Pods, labelled app: store and track: stable.
blocks.why: With one canary Pod beside them, the canary gets about one request in ten.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because apps/v1 Deployments must have a selector.
blocks.comment: Nine copies of the stable version
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: store-stable
spec:
  replicas: 9
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: store
      track: stable

blocks.title: Describe the stable Pods
blocks.what: Each Pod gets app: store and track: stable.
blocks.why: The Service selects only app: store, so it reaches both tracks.
blocks.ifRemoved: The Deployment would have nothing to create, so Kubernetes rejects it.
blocks.comment: Label each Pod as store and stable
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: store-stable
spec:
  replicas: 9
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: store
      track: stable
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: store
        track: stable

blocks.title: A page that says stable
blocks.what: busybox writes a page saying stable, then serves it on port 80.
blocks.why: Counting the answers shows how traffic is shared.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the Deployment, because its Pods would have nothing to run.
blocks.comment: A small web server that answers stable
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: store-stable
spec:
  replicas: 9
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: store
      track: stable
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: store
        track: stable
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "mkdir -p /www && echo stable > /www/index.html && exec httpd -f -p 80 -h /www"]

blocks.title: Add the Service
blocks.what: Three dashes start a second object: a Service called store.
blocks.why: Clients use the name store and never choose a version themselves.
blocks.ifRemoved: Clients would have to find the Pods themselves.
blocks.comment: A second object: the Service clients use
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: store-stable
spec:
  replicas: 9
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: store
      track: stable
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: store
        track: stable
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "mkdir -p /www && echo stable > /www/index.html && exec httpd -f -p 80 -h /www"]
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: store

blocks.title: Send traffic to every store Pod
blocks.what: The selector names only app: store, not the track.
blocks.why: Each request goes to one matching Pod, so traffic splits by Pod count.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the Service, because it must say which port to listen on.
blocks.comment: Traffic goes to every store Pod, stable or canary
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: store-stable
spec:
  replicas: 9
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: store
      track: stable
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: store
        track: stable
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "mkdir -p /www && echo stable > /www/index.html && exec httpd -f -p 80 -h /www"]
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: store
spec:
  selector:
    app: store
  ports:
    - port: 80

blocks.title: Add the canary
blocks.what: Three dashes start a third object: the Deployment for the canary, the new version.
blocks.why: It runs beside stable behind the same Service.
blocks.comment: A third object: the canary Deployment
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: store-stable
spec:
  replicas: 9
  selector:
    matchLabels:

  template:
    metadata:

        app: store

    spec:

        - name: web

---
apiVersion: v1

apiVersion: apps/v1

blocks.title: One canary Pod
blocks.what: Keep one canary Pod, labelled app: store and track: canary.
blocks.why: One Pod out of ten gets about 10% of requests. Raise it as confidence grows.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because apps/v1 Deployments must have a selector.
blocks.comment: One copy of the canary version
blocks.yaml:

kind: Deployment

blocks.comment: Label the Pod as store and canary

notes.---: Three dashes separate objects. One file can hold several objects.
notes.apiVersion: The API version. Deployments are in apps/v1. Services are in the core v1 API.
notes.Deployment:kind: The type of object to create. A Deployment keeps identical Pods running.
notes.Service:kind: The type of object to create. A Service sends traffic to Pods with chosen labels.
notes.metadata: Details that identify the object, such as its name.
notes.Deployment:metadata.name: The Deployment’s name. Its Pods get names that start with it.
notes.Service:metadata.name: The Service name. Clients inside the cluster use http://store.
notes.Deployment:spec: The desired state of this Deployment.
notes.Service:spec: The desired state: which Pods get traffic, on which port.
notes.spec.selector: Which Pods this Deployment manages. It cannot change after creation.
notes.Service:spec.selector: Pods must have all of these labels to receive traffic.
notes.spec.selector.matchLabels: Pods must have all of these labels to be managed by this Deployment.
notes.spec.selector.matchLabels.app: The app label shared by both versions: store.
notes.spec.template: The Pod template: the blueprint for every Pod this Deployment creates.
notes.spec.template.metadata: Details given to every Pod created from the template.
notes.spec.template.metadata.labels: Labels given to every Pod. They must match the selector.
notes.spec.template.metadata.labels.app: Every Pod of both versions gets app: store.
notes.spec.template.spec: What each Pod runs. This is the same spec as in a Pod file.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers: The containers in each Pod. Each list item starts with a dash.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].name: The container’s name. It must be unique within the Pod.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].image: A tiny image with basic shell tools, pinned to a version.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].command: Write a page naming the version, then serve it on port 80 with busybox’s web server.
notes.spec.selector.app: Send traffic to Pods labelled app: store.
notes.spec.ports: The ports the Service listens on. Each list item is one port.
notes.spec.ports[].port: Listen on port 80 and forward to port 80 on the Pods.
notes.spec.replicas: How many Pods of this version to run. The ratio sets the traffic share.

tryIt.result: Creates store-stable, the store Service, and store-canary.
READY shows 9/9 for stable and 1/1 for the canary.

tryIt.command: kubectl run client --rm -i --restart=Never --image=busybox:1.37.0 -- sh -c 'for i in $(seq 100); do wget -qO- http://store; done | sort | uniq -c'
tryIt.result: Counts 100 answers. Roughly 10 say canary and 90 say stable. The split varies a little each time.
Promotes the canary a step: 3 of 12 Pods, about a quarter of requests.
Removes both Deployments and the Service.

questions.question: Why does the Service selector leave out track?
answers: So it sends traffic to both stable and canary Pods
questions.explain: A Service reaches every Pod with all its selector labels. Leaving out track includes both versions.

questions.question: About what share of requests reaches the canary?
questions.explain: One canary Pod beside nine stable ones gets about one request in ten.

questions.question: The canary looks good. What is the next step?
answers: Raise canary replicas and lower stable, step by step
questions.explain: Shifting Pods a few at a time moves traffic gradually until the new version takes over.
